reviewed.adw-avatar-icon: A hook on the avatar's fallback symbolic, which sits beside the base `adw-icon` rather than replacing it. It carries no look for the same reason `adw-icon` carries none — the glyph is a bitmap already rasterised in its fill colour at its box size, and NativeScript drops a CSS value for a property the widget set as a LOCAL one, which `GtkImage` does for width and height. Colour and size come from `iconColor` / `iconSize`, both driven from the avatar's own palette entry and diameter; what a rule could still add here is margin or opacity.
reviewed.adw-bottom-sheet: The sheet host. Its only painted child node in libadwaita is `> dimming`, the scrim (_bottom-sheet.scss:2-4), which this port does not draw at all — the NS subset has no z-index or backdrop, and the widget's header says so. The panel is `.adw-bottom-sheet-panel`.
reviewed.adw-bottom-sheet-content: A marker stamped on the view handed to `setContent`, and the reason `addMarkerClass` exists — it is how the widget finds that layer again to strip the class when the content is replaced.
reviewed.adw-bottom-sheet-sheet: A marker stamped on the view handed to `setSheet`. It sits INSIDE `.adw-bottom-sheet-panel`, which is the node libadwaita calls `sheet` and the node this theme paints.
reviewed.adw-carousel: The pager host — a grid holding the scroller and the dots. libadwaita ships no stylesheet for AdwCarousel: the dots are drawn in C from the foreground colour (adw-carousel-indicator-dots.c) and the pages paint themselves, so there is no node here for a rule to answer.
reviewed.adw-carousel-page: A marker stamped on a view the consumer supplies, so an app can reach its own pages. Its width is the carousel's `pageWidth`, assigned as a local value — which a CSS width could not override anyway.
reviewed.adw-carousel-track: The horizontal box of pages inside the scroller. It only holds them side by side at the width each page is given; `.adw-carousel-scroller` already declares the transparent surface behind it.
reviewed.adw-entry-row: The row's own base class, and the carrier for the `focused` / `empty` state classes that ride on the same string. Everything libadwaita puts on `row.entry` itself is either unreachable here (a focus-ring, a `:disabled` filter) or already applied: its 6px header margin pairs with the editable area's 6px padding (_lists.scss:186-192) for the same 12 inset `.adw-row` gives every row.
reviewed.adw-entry-row-suffixes: The box holding indicator, apply button and pencil. `AdwActionRow.setSuffix` also stamps `.adw-row-suffix`, which places and vertically centres it, and libadwaita puts no spacing on the box either — the 6 between the three rides on the children (_lists.scss:200-203).
reviewed.adw-expander-row: A row host. `expander-widget` carries a focus-ring and nothing else (_expanders.scss:12-25); the paint is on the chevron (`.adw-expander-toggle`) and on the revealed box (`.adw-expander-disclosure`), both styled.
reviewed.adw-icon: The base class of every decorative symbolic icon, and the class a CSS rule can say the LEAST about: a GtkImage is an Image showing a bitmap already rendered in its fill colour and size, and NativeScript drops a CSS value for any property the widget set as a LOCAL one (properties/index.js:585-598) — which GtkImage does for width and height. So `color`, `font-size`, `width` and `height` are all inert on it; what a rule can still carry is margin, opacity and background. Before treating a missing look here as a gap, check whether it belongs in `iconColor` / `iconSize` instead.
reviewed.adw-inline-view-switcher: The switcher host. Every rule libadwaita writes under `inline-view-switcher` is a descendant selector on `> toggle-group` (_toggle-group.scss:227-256) — the pill bar, which is `.adw-inline-view-switcher-bar` here, and its toggles.
reviewed.adw-insensitive: A styling hook with no look of its own: the applier sets NS_INSENSITIVE_OPACITY on the pencil imperatively, which is what the user sees (entry-row-view.ts, applyEntryRowState).
reviewed.adw-menu-button: A marker on an AdwImageButton subclass. `Adw.MenuButton` in a header bar IS a flat icon button, so the base class carries the whole look; the class exists so an app can reach its own menu buttons.
reviewed.adw-password-entry-row: A subclass marker. C adds a bare `password` class to the row (adw-password-entry-row.c:173); every rule that selects it lands on descendants this port styles by their own class — the caps-lock dim is `> .indicator`, which `.adw-entry-indicator` now carries.
reviewed.adw-password-peek: The reveal/conceal toggle. C builds it `flat` (adw-password-entry-row.c:151), which is what `.adw-image-button` already is; the icon it swaps between is a bitmap the widget renders, not something a rule could pick.
reviewed.adw-preferences-group-labels: The title + description column. libadwaita gives `box.labels` one property, `border-spacing: 6px` (_preferences.scss:7-9), and the NS subset has no spacing — so the 6 rides on `.adw-preferences-group-description`'s top margin. Its own placement is the grid column and `verticalAlignment`, both set in the widget.
reviewed.adw-preferences-group-suffix: A wrapper this port invented to place the header suffix in grid column 1 — libadwaita adds the suffix straight to `header_box` (adw-preferences-group.c:598-617) and puts no spacing on that box. The column and the middle alignment are set in the widget, so there is nothing left for a rule to say.
reviewed.adw-row-flush-top: An ancestor-scoped rule, deliberately: `.boxed-list .adw-row-flush-top` (theme/adwaita.css) is the only one, and the only writer is `AdwPreferencesGroup._refreshRowEdges()`, which toggles it on the FIRST row of its own listbox — a node that is a `.boxed-list` descendant by construction. It exists because the NS CSS subset has no `:first-child`, so the flush top edge cannot be selected; outside a boxed list the class would have nothing to flush against.
reviewed.adw-shortcut-label-disabled: A consumer hook so the no-shortcut state can be styled without matching on child count. The look comes from the .dimmed half of the same className, which the theme does style.
reviewed.adw-shortcut-label-keys: One combination's box. It carries no paint — the 6-unit border-spacing between keycaps rides on the caps themselves via adw-shortcut-label-spaced, because the NS subset has no :first-child.
reviewed.adw-spin-minus: Which end of the stepper this button is. Both carry `.adw-spin-button`, which is what libadwaita styles — one rule covers `button.up` and `button.down` alike (_lists.scss:250-259) — and the difference between them is the symbolic icon, set in the widget.
reviewed.adw-spin-plus: The counterpart of adw-spin-minus: same shared rule, same reason.
reviewed.adw-spin-row: A row host. Everything under `row.spin` (_lists.scss:240-262) selects the spinbutton subtree, which this port renders as `.adw-spin-control` / `.adw-spin-button` / `.adw-spin-value` and styles there. What is left on the host is a focus-ring and a `:disabled` filter, neither of which the NS subset can express.
reviewed.adw-spinner-ring: The platform ActivityIndicator inside the spinner box. Its diameter is computed by `spinnerGeometry` and assigned as a local width/height, and its colour is `color` INHERITED from `.adw-spinner` — colorProperty is an InheritedCssProperty (style-properties.js:1008) and ActivityIndicator honours it on both platforms. The parent selector genuinely carries the rule.
reviewed.adw-split-button: The host of the two halves, and a marker with no paint of its own. Every rule that mentions it uses it as an ANCESTOR — `.adw-split-button.flat .adw-split-button-action` and its dropdown twin — because that is where `.flat` is read from; the surfaces are `.adw-split-button-action` / `-dropdown`, both styled, and libadwaita's own `splitbutton` node carries only the linked-button plumbing this port renders as a grid.
reviewed.adw-split-button-action-icon: The optional glyph in the action half — a GtkImage, so see adw-icon: its fill follows the colour scheme through `iconColor` and its alignment is set in the widget. The surface under it is `.adw-split-button-action`.
reviewed.adw-split-button-chevron: The dropdown arrow. Same as adw-split-button-action-icon — a GtkImage centred by the widget on the `.adw-split-button-dropdown` cell, whose direction-dependent glyph comes from `splitButtonArrowSvg`.
reviewed.adw-switch-row: A row host whose whole look is `.adw-row` + `.adw-action-row` plus the switch in its suffix. libadwaita has no `row.switch` selector at all — AdwSwitchRow is an action row with a GtkSwitch as its activatable widget (adw-switch-row.c), and the switch's accent is `.adw-switch`.
reviewed.adw-tab-view: The container holding the tab strip and the pages. libadwaita's `tabview` selector carries exactly one declaration, `box-shadow: none` while a drop is active (_tab-view.scss:300-304); the strip's chrome is `tabbar .box`, which this port renders as `.adw-tab-view-bar`, and the page surface comes from whatever the app puts in it.
reviewed.adw-toast-overlay: The overlay host. In libadwaita the paint is entirely on the `toast` node — background, 150px radius, padding, margins (_misc.scss:38-70) — which is `.adw-toast` here; `toastoverlay` has no rule of its own, being a bare container over the content.
reviewed.adw-toast-overlay-content: A marker stamped on the consumer's content layer so an app can reach it. The overlay only assigns it the grid cell under the toast strip.
reviewed.adw-wrap-box: A layout, not a surface — AdwWrapBox is a layout with no dedicated scss, and libadwaita indeed ships none. Direction, wrapping, justification and the child/line spacing are all properties, applied to the FlexboxLayout and its children by `_applyLayout` / `_applyChildren`.
reviewed.keycap: Scoped on purpose, and the one unprefixed name this port keeps verbatim from libadwaita: `.adw-shortcut-label .keycap` is the only rule, and `SHORTCUT_LABEL_KEYCAP_CLASS` is set nowhere but inside `AdwShortcutLabel`'s own cap boxes. A cap outside a shortcut label has no meaning to be styled — and renaming this constant is the incident the whole gate was written for.
